model: Life insurer FCFE (net free surplus generation) at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 IFRS 17 total revenue per 1299.HK_Metrics.csv (insurance revenue plus investment result as presented in the consolidated income statement). It is the scale line the margin paths are mapped onto, not the economic driver: AIA's own volume measure is Total Weighted Premium Income (US$46.9bn FY2025, H1 2026 TWPI 27,526 +15% AER) and its value measure is VONB (US$5,516m FY2025; H1 2026 3,212 +13% AER). H1 2026 revenue 11,686 vs 10,463 (+11.7%). FY2022-FY2025 are IFRS 17 restated; FY2017-FY2021 are IFRS 4 and not comparable (FY2021 34,444 -> FY2022 16,319 is the accounting break, not a collapse).
inputs.share_count_basis: 10,347m ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim, financial summary line 1515) plus ~18m dilutive share awards (H1 2026 weighted diluted 10,439 vs basic 10,421, OPAT per share table) = 10,365m fully diluted. The FY2025-results buyback (US$1,743m) was fully executed inside H1 2026 (free-surplus table: share buy-backs 1,743), so no further programme is in flight at the valuation date. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows and share awards are satisfied with purchased shares (ShareAwardSettlement US$89m FY2025); the buyback programme (US$2,279m FY2025, US$4,150m FY2024) is a use of the net FSG being capitalised, not extra growth. Count fell 11,734 (FY2022) -> 10,347 (Jun-26), ~3.5%/yr.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the bank/insurer convention in this folder (PRU, MET, GL, IAG.AX, 0998.HK). Borrowings of US$13,892m at 30 June 2026 are medium-term notes and subordinated securities that form part of the regulatory capital stack; their coupons (interest paid on MTNs and securities US$551m FY2025) sit inside OPAT and inside the 'finance costs and other capital movements' line (US$562m FY2025) that net FSG is struck after. Deducting the debt again would charge it twice. Consolidated cash of US$7,783m is general-account and policyholder liquidity, not shareholder surplus. Free surplus of US$10,470m at 30 June 2026 (excess of adjusted net worth over required capital, SCR 210%) is NOT added as a bridge item: it is the buffer that lets the Group absorb capital-market stress and fund new business, management has not set a public floor for it, and H1 2026 shareholder returns of US$3,649m (132% of net FSG) already drew it down from 10,972. Conservative by up to US$1.01/share (HK$7.9) if the market treats all of it as surplus.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 NET FREE SURPLUS GENERATION (net FSG) US$4,451m = UFSG 6,765 - free surplus used to fund new business 1,437 - unallocated Group Office expenses 315 - finance costs and other capital movements 562 (FY2025 annual report, free-surplus table at line 2561). This is the cash the Group can actually pay out: AIA's capital policy returns 75% of net FSG via dividends and buybacks (FY2025 actual returns 4,706 = 106% including the extra US$1.0bn buyback after the capital review). Net FSG history: FY2023 3,932, FY2024 4,020, FY2025 4,451 (+14% per share), H1 2026 2,758 vs H1 2025 2,430 (+13% AER, +12% per share). Conversion of OPAT to net FSG: FY2025 4,451 / 7,136 = 62.4%; H1 2026 2,758 / 4,163 = 66.3%. An insurer's OCF-less-capex (CSV free_cash_flow 6,521 FY2025) is not free cash, so the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied.
inputs.sbc_source: 1299.HK_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 US$103m (cash-flow statement share-based payment add-back; FY2024 84, FY2023 72, H1 2026 61). No net-share-settlement withholding is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0); awards are satisfied with shares bought in the market (ShareAwardSettlement 89 FY2025), which is the cash form of the same cost. Charged at 0.48% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: Share buy-backs US$2,279m FY2025 (FY2024 4,150; FY2023 3,637; FY2022 3,570); US$1,743m in H1 2026 completing the programme approved with the FY2025 results. Dividends paid US$2,441m FY2025; H1 2026 1,930 (final FY2025 dividend 144.08 HK cents, +10%). Interim FY2026 dividend 53.90 HK cents (+10%).
inputs.fx_note: USD/HKD 7.8476 (HKD per USD) from Yahoo Finance HKD=X at 2026-10-16T08:13:06Z; the Hong Kong dollar is pegged in a 7.75-7.85 band under the Linked Exchange Rate System. fx_rate is model -> quote: the USD per-share values are multiplied by 7.8476 to reach the HKD quote. Parity check: the US OTC ADR AAGIY (1 ADR = 4 ordinary shares) closed US$37.20 on 2026-10-15 = US$9.30/share = HK$72.98 at 7.8476, against the HK$73.20 HKEX close on 2026-10-16 -- within 0.3%. AIA files in USD (statements headed 'US$ millions') and quotes in HKD on the HKEX; same pattern as 0288.HK and 1258.HK.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T07:58:06Z, HKEX closing session (Yahoo Finance chart API; HKEX closes 08:00Z). Regular-session print, not after-hours.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.0% on USD flows: 10-year US Treasury ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 = ~9.7%, rounded up to 10.0% for the Hong Kong / Mainland China concentration (60% of VONB) and the regulatory tail shown by the mid-2026 Mainland tax-enforcement episode and the 2019 Hong Kong disruption. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC, because net FSG is post-interest FCFE. Same rate in all three scenarios; scenario risk sits in the driver paths and weights. Cross-reference: AIA's own EV risk discount rates are ~8-9.25% by market, so 10% is deliberately above the rate at which the Group discounts its own in-force book; the required_return_table shows the 9% row. Against PRU (10.0%) and MET (9.5%) in this folder: AIA carries less balance-sheet spread risk and a stronger franchise, but more political/regulatory risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities are US$483m (FY2025 note) against US$345bn of assets; the lease charge is inside the OPAT expense base and inside UFSG.
inputs.nci_treatment: None in the flows or bridge: OPAT of US$7,136m (FY2025) and 4,163 (H1 2026) is the figure attributable to shareholders of the Company (the kpis UnderlyingProfitAfterTax series 7,171 / 4,184 includes the US$35-41m NCI share). Net FSG is a shareholder measure by construction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a pan-Asian life insurer, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the PRU / MET / GL / IAG.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent. The dcf-methods routing default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because (1) IFRS book is not a usable compounding base for a life insurer under IFRS 17: shareholders' equity fell from US$60.5bn (IFRS 4, FY2021) to US$44.7bn (IFRS 17 restated FY2022) because the CSM (US$67.8bn at 30 June 2026, the stock of unearned future profit) sits in liabilities, and book per share (US$3.93) has gone sideways while the business compounded; (2) AIA does not retain book -- it distributes ~75-100% of net FSG and the value driver is the free surplus the in-force book throws off. EARNINGS ANCHOR: OPAT (operating profit after tax), management's segment measure, which strips short-term investment fluctuations and other non-operating items; the FCFE is net free surplus generation, the EV-basis cash measure management uses to set dividends and buybacks. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = IFRS 17 total revenue (CSV); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax OPAT BEFORE share-based compensation as % of revenue (FY2025: 7,136 / 0.84 + 103 = 8,598 / 21,618 = 39.8%); sbc_pct_path 0.48%; da_pct_path 0 (D&A is inside the expense base, no PP&E capex of note); cash_tax_rate_path 17% (effective tax rate on an operating-profit basis 16% in FY2025, 17% in H1 2026, both including the notional Pillar Two GMT top-up tax, per management guidance), so (margin - SBC) x (1 - tax) = OPAT; capex_pct_path = free surplus RETAINED (new-business strain, Group Office costs, finance costs, i.e. OPAT minus net FSG), set so that FCFE = the scenario's net-FSG conversion of OPAT (FY2025 actual 62.4%, H1 2026 66.3%). wc_capture 0. EMBEDDED VALUE CROSS-CHECK: EV Equity US$83,402m at 30 June 2026 = US$8.06/share = HK$63.3 (kpis EVEquity FY2020 67,185 -> FY2025 79,678; per share 5yr CAGR 6.4%); the price is 1.16x EV. Operating ROEV 15.8% FY2025 / 18.0% annualised H1 2026 at a 10% cost of equity and ~3% long-run growth brackets a justified P/EV of ~1.8x on a Gordon basis, but EV already discounts VIF at AIA's 8-9% RDRs, so the base FCFE value landing at roughly 1.0-1.1x EV says the house method is pricing the in-force book at a higher discount rate than AIA does and giving limited credit for future VONB beyond the 10-year horizon -- that is the conservative bias by design. CSM: US$67.8bn at 30 June 2026 releasing at ~9.2%/yr into OPAT; new business CSM 4,869 in H1 2026 (+11%). CAPITAL: shareholder capital ratio 210% at 30 June 2026 (221% FY2025, 236% FY2024), free surplus 10,470; D-SII designation October 2025 with no stated change to capital policy.
inputs.guidance_treatment: Management's 2023-2026 target is a 9-11% OPAT-per-share CAGR (CER, net of GMT); at H1 2026 (+13% per share) it 'now expects to exceed' it. Roughly 3%/yr of per-share growth comes from the buyback, so absolute OPAT growth of 10-12% in FY2026 is what the guidance implies; base takes +12% absolute (H1 +15% AER was USD-weakness flattered; CER +11%). No numerical guidance exists beyond FY2026; the Mainland China new-region 40% VONB CAGR to 2030 is from a US$118m base and is inside the growth paths, not modelled separately.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: OPAT-per-share 3yr CAGR 7.7% (FY2022 0.541 -> FY2025 0.677) and EV-Equity-per-share 3yr/5yr CAGRs 7.7%/6.4% are the compounding measures for a life insurer; IFRS 17 revenue 3yr CAGR 9.8% is the top end; equity CAGRs are broken by the IFRS 17 transition and buybacks
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (-1.1% 3yr, -7.3% 5yr) are an accounting artefact: IFRS 17 moved ~US$16bn of equity into the CSM liability on transition (FY2021 60,467 -> FY2022 restated 44,672) and US$12.6bn of buybacks since FY2022 have retired 12% of the shares. EPS 3yr CAGR (28.2%, FY2022 0.28 -> FY2025 0.59) is flattered by a depressed FY2022 base (reported net profit swings with short-term investment fluctuations: 3,331 / 3,764 / 6,836 / 6,234 FY2022-25). No owner-FCF series exists for an insurer, so FCF CAGRs are null; net FSG and OPAT are the cash and earnings series.

base.narrative: FY2026: revenue +10% (H1 +11.7%, H2 against a stronger comparative), OPAT +12% absolute to ~US$8.0bn = (41.0% - 0.48%) x 83% of 23,780 -- H1 4,163 plus an H2 of ~3.83bn, i.e. above the 9-11% per-share target management now expects to exceed once the ~3% buyback contribution is added back. Net FSG conversion 62.5% (FY2025 62.4%; H1 2026 66.3% is seasonally high) rising to 65% by FY2031 as the shift to less capital-intensive participating products (new-business strain -6% in FY2025, +4% in H1 2026 against VONB +10%) continues; net FSG FY2026 ~US$5.0bn. FY2027-30: growth 8 -> 6% as Hong Kong Mainland Visitor Business normalises from +35% and Thailand works through the co-payment change; margin drifts 41.0 -> 41.5% on CSM release compounding (9.2% release rate) and the 10%/yr unit-cost reduction. FY2031-35: 5.5 -> 3.5%. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3.0% = 14.7x, 15x FCFE); Gordon binds.

bull.narrative: Mainland Visitor Business keeps growing through the tax-enforcement noise (as it did in H1 2026), AIA China's nine new provinces deliver the 40% VONB CAGR, China Post Life compounds, and Thailand recovers from FY2027. Revenue 11 -> 4% over ten years; OPAT margin to 42.5% (CSM release plus unit-cost gains and healthcare claims savings of ~US$300m/yr). Conversion rises 63% -> 70% by FY2031 as participating products displace capital-heavy guarantees. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3.5% = 15.9x, 17x); Gordon binds.

bear.narrative: Mainland China enforces the 20% tax on Hong Kong participating-policy dividends and tightens capital outflows, so Mainland Visitor Business (the driver of Hong Kong's +28% VONB in FY2025) shrinks from FY2027; Thailand's co-payment regime and further local reserving changes bite; falling China rates force more economic-assumption VONB markdowns. FY2026 is already largely banked (+8%), then revenue growth 2-3%. OPAT margin slips to 39.0% as new-business CSM slows and the release rate carries a smaller book. Conversion stays at 60% (below FY2025's 62.4%) because strain does not fall with volume and regulatory capital (ICS alignment, D-SII) rises. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2.5% = 13.7x, 13x); cap binds.

scenario_narratives.base: A pan-Asian life insurer whose in-force book (CSM US$67.8bn) releases ~9% a year into operating profit, with new business adding to that stock faster than it runs off. Net free surplus of ~US$5.0bn in FY2026 grows at 7-8% for a few years as Hong Kong Mainland Visitor demand normalises from a 35% spike, then at mid-single digits, with a little more of each dollar of OPAT becoming distributable as the product mix shifts toward participating. Discounted at a 10% cost of equity that is a point above the rate AIA uses on its own in-force book, the result sits close to the price: the market is paying a fair price for the franchise, not a bargain.
scenario_narratives.bull: The three China vectors -- Mainland Visitor Business in Hong Kong, AIA China's new-province expansion and the China Post Life stake -- all compound, the healthcare and digital programmes keep taking cost out, and the capital-light product shift lifts conversion to 70%. AIA re-rates from 1.16x EV toward its pre-2022 range.
scenario_narratives.bear: Beijing makes Hong Kong policies structurally less attractive to Mainland buyers and the Group's largest growth engine stalls; Thailand and local capital rules trim margin and lift strain. Earnings grow at 2-3% from a FY2026 base that is already banked and the stock settles at a low-growth insurer multiple.

probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is degenerate: SBC is 0.48% of revenue so house and street values are HK$1.5 apart (weighted 65.99 vs 67.43) and the price sits far outside that band; treat the band as collapsed, as in SBC-zero markets, and read weighted_iv alone.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: 60% of VONB comes from Hong Kong and Mainland China, the mid-2026 Mainland tax-enforcement reports knocked the shares 9% in a day and HSBC cut its target on structural grounds, and the 2019 Hong Kong episode shows how fast Mainland Visitor Business can shut. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the China expansion, the Hong Kong cross-border flow and a 70% conversion rate AIA has not yet delivered to arrive together. Same 25/50/25 as PRU and MET, the closest cost-of-equity comparables in the folder.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value AIA on the free surplus its in-force book actually generates for shareholders (net FSG, the figure that funds the 75% payout policy), discounted at a 10% cost of equity with the MTN capital stack left inside the flows and no credit for the US$10.5bn free-surplus buffer. Earnings are built from OPAT, the operating measure, and the FCFE conversion is set to what AIA has delivered (62-66% of OPAT), so new-business strain is charged in full. Embedded Value (US$8.06/share, HK$63.3) and operating ROEV (16-18%) are the cross-check, not the driver; the FCFE route values the business at roughly 1.0-1.1x EV, below the 1.16x the market pays and well below an appraisal-value approach that capitalises VONB.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hong Kong Mainland Visitor Business: Beijing tax enforcement on participating-policy dividends, capital-outflow controls or cross-border travel disruption would hit the Group's largest growth engine; bear models a stall from FY2027

Interest rates and equity markets: a 50bp rate move is ~0.4-0.8% of EV and a 10% equity move ~3.6%; falling China rates have already forced VONB markdowns; these flow through investment return variances outside net FSG but into free surplus
Regulatory capital: ICS alignment across seven markets, the D-SII designation and ad hoc local reserving changes (Thailand -US$169m in FY2025) can raise required capital and cut conversion
Currency: USD reporting against a basket of HKD, RMB, THB, SGD and MYR earnings; CER and AER growth have diverged by 3-4 points in recent periods
Capital-return pace: the shareholder capital ratio has fallen 236% -> 221% -> 210% in 18 months; if the buffer is rebuilt, payout drops below 75% of net FSG for a period
Free surplus of US$10.5bn is not credited; if it is genuinely surplus the valuation is ~HK$7.9/share too low

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 68.00-92.15 HKD. USD/HKD from Yahoo HKD=X at the time in inputs.fx_note; ADR parity via AAGIY (1 ADR = 4 shares).
data_sources.financials: 1299.HK_Metrics.csv and the 1299.HK.duckdb kpis table (EVEquity, UnderlyingProfitAfterTax, ShareRepurchases, DividendsPaid, BookValuePerShare, InsuranceServiceResult); 1299.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (free-surplus table line 2561, OPAT/ETR guidance line 1715, borrowings 2196, shares 2120, diluted shares 12770); 1299.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (financial summary lines 102-146, OPAT and diluted shares 1130-1137, CSM movement 1147-1176, free-surplus table 1790-1806, shares in issue 1515).
data_sources.qualitative: 1299.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-16): guidance (9-11% OPAT per share CAGR 2023-26, 75% net FSG payout, 40% new-region VONB CAGR), the August 2026 Mainland tax-enforcement episode, D-SII designation, Thailand co-payment regulation, China Post Life stake.
